function.name: clarify
function.description:
Ask the user a question when you need clarification, feedback, or a decision before proceeding. Two modes: multiple choice (up to 4 `choices`; the UI auto-appends a 5th 'Other — type your answer' option) or open-ended (omit `choices`; user types free-form text).
CRITICAL: put options ONLY in the `choices` array — NEVER enumerate them inside `question`. The UI renders `choices` as selectable rows; options written into the question string are dead prose the user can't pick. Right: question='Which deployment target?', choices=['staging','prod']. Wrong: question='Which target? 1) staging 2) prod', choices=[].
Use when: the task is ambiguous, a decision has meaningful trade-offs, you want post-task feedback, or you offer to save a skill / update memory. Do NOT use for yes/no confirmation of dangerous commands (the terminal tool handles that). When stakes are low, make a reasonable default choice yourself.

question.description: The question text ONLY (e.g. 'Which deployment target?') — never embed answer options here; pass them in `choices`.

choices.description: REQUIRED whenever presenting selectable options: one option per element, max 4. UI renders them as pickable rows and auto-appends 'Other (type your answer)'. Omit entirely ONLY for a genuinely open-ended free-text question.

function.name: memory
function.description:
Save durable facts to persistent memory that survive across sessions. Memory is injected into every future turn — keep entries compact and high-signal.
HOW: make ALL changes in ONE call via the 'operations' array (items: {action, content?, old_text?}). The batch applies atomically and the char limit is checked only on the FINAL result, so one call can remove/replace stale entries to free room AND add new ones even when the add alone would overflow. The response reports current/limit chars and confirms completion — one batch finishes the update, do not repeat it. Bare action/content/old_text fields are for a single lone change only.
WHEN: save proactively on user preferences, corrections, personal details, or stable facts about their environment, conventions, workflow. Priority: preferences & corrections > environment facts > procedures. The best memory stops the user repeating themselves.
IF FULL: the add is rejected and current entries are shown — reissue ONE batch that removes/shortens stale entries and adds the new one together.
TARGETS: 'user' = who the user is (name, role, preferences, style); 'memory' = your notes (environment, conventions, tool quirks, lessons).
SKIP: trivial/obvious or easily re-discovered facts, raw data dumps, task progress, completed-work logs, temporary TODO state (use session_search for those). Reusable procedures belong in a skill, not memory.

action.description: Single-op shape only; omit when using 'operations'.

content.description: Entry content; required for 'add' and 'replace' (single-op shape).

old_text.description: Short unique substring identifying the existing entry. REQUIRED for 'replace' and 'remove' (single-op shape); omit only for 'add'.

operations.description: Batch shape: operations applied atomically in one call against the final char budget — preferred for multiple changes or consolidating to free room. Items: {action, content?, old_text?}.

old_text.description: Substring identifying the entry for replace/remove.

function.name: skills_list
function.description: List available skills (name + description). Use skill_view(name) to load full content.

category.description: Optional category filter to narrow results

function.name: text_to_speech
function.description: Convert text to speech audio. Returns a MEDIA: path the platform delivers as native audio — a voice bubble on compatible providers (e.g. Telegram), otherwise a regular attachment; CLI mode saves to ~/voice-memos/. Voice and provider are user-configured (built-in providers like edge/openai, or custom command providers under tts.providers.<name>), not model-selected.

text.description: Text to speak. Provider character caps are enforced automatically (OpenAI 4096, xAI 15000, MiniMax 10000, ElevenLabs 5k-40k depending on model); over-long input is truncated.

function.name: todo
function.description: Session task list. Use for complex tasks with 3+ steps or when the user gives multiple tasks. Call with no parameters to read the current list; pass 'todos' to create/update. merge=false (default) replaces the entire list with a fresh plan; merge=true updates existing items by id and adds new ones. Item shape: {id, content, status: pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled}. List order is priority; only ONE item in_progress at a time; mark items completed immediately when done; if something fails, cancel it and add a revised item. Always returns the full current list.

todos.description: Items to write; omit to read the current list.

merge.description: true: update existing items by id, add new ones. false (default): replace the entire list.

function.name: vision_analyze
function.description: Load an image into the conversation so you can see it. Accepts an http(s) URL, local file path, or data: URL. When the active model has native vision, the image attaches directly to your context and you read the pixels yourself next turn — call this whenever the user references an image (filepath in their message, URL in tool output, browser screenshot, etc.). Non-vision models fall back to an auxiliary vision model that returns a text description.

image_url.description: Image http/https URL, local file path, or data: URL.

question.description: Your specific question or request about the image; used as context on the next turn after the image is seen.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for information. Returns up to 5 results by default with titles, URLs, and descriptions. The query is passed through to the configured backend, so operators such as site:domain, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, and "exact phrase" may work when the backend supports them.

query.description: The search query to look up on the web. You may include backend-supported operators such as site:example.com, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, or "exact phrase".

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

function.name: tool_search
function.description: Search 23 additional tools that are loaded on demand. Returns up to ``limit`` matches with name and description. Follow with `tool_describe` to load a tool's full parameter schema, then `tool_call` to invoke it. Tools listed at the top of this system prompt are already available and do not need to be searched. Deferred tools available via this router: browser_back, browser_click, browser_console, browser_get_images, browser_navigate, browser_press, browser_scroll, browser_snapshot, browser_type, browser_vision, cronjob, delegate_task, execute_code, patch, process, read_file, search_files, session_search, skill_manage, skill_view, terminal, web_extract, write_file.

query.description: Keywords describing the capability you need (e.g. 'create github issue').

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default 5.

function.name: tool_describe
function.description: Load the full JSON schema for one tool returned by `tool_search`. Required before `tool_call` if the tool's parameters are unknown.

name.description: Exact tool name (as returned by tool_search).

function.name: tool_call
function.description: Invoke a deferred tool by name. EXACT shape: {"name": "terminal", "arguments": {"command": "echo hi"}} — top-level "name" is the tool to invoke and the tool's OWN parameters go INSIDE the "arguments" object. Never nest another "name" or "arguments" wrapper inside "arguments". Argument shape matches the tool's schema (see tool_describe). Policy, hooks, and approvals run exactly as for any directly-listed tool.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, matching its schema.
